findings.title: Removing the global lock from BuildIndex creates a race where concurrent builds for the same key return different indexes and leak one
findings.body: The PR removes the `b.cacheMu.Lock()` held for the entire `BuildIndex` and only locks the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. Two goroutines can now concurrently call `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` key (e.g. `searchSupport.init` spawns one goroutine per namespace via errgroup, and `getOrCreateIndex` can also trigger `build` for the same key from a Search request or a watch event). Both will create separate bleve indexes (memory or on-disk), both will run the full builder, and the second one to finish will overwrite `b.cache[key]`, orphaning the first index. The orphaned index is never closed, leaking file handles/memory, and worse, callers that already obtained the first index (e.g. an in-flight `Search` or the `handleEvent` goroutine holding `index` from `getOrCreateIndex`) will write/delete documents into an index that is no longer reachable via `GetIndex`, so watch-event updates are silently lost and search results become inconsistent. Additionally, for the file-based path, two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, ...)` calls on the same directory can corrupt the on-disk index. The fix requires per-key locking (e.g. a `singleflight.Group` keyed by `NamespacedResource`, or a map of per-key mutexes) so that only one build happens per key and concurrent callers wait for and share the same index.

findings.body: `TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` now writes `b.cache[key] = idx` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. Concurrent map iteration and map write in Go is a fatal runtime error ("concurrent map iteration and map write"), which can crash the process. `TotalDocs` is called from `searchSupport.init` (search.go line 216) after `group.Wait()`, but also potentially from metrics/health paths while other goroutines (watch event handlers calling `getOrCreateIndex` -> `build` -> `BuildIndex`) are still inserting into the map. The map must be accessed under `cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`.

There is no cancellation tied to server shutdown (`server.Stop` only calls `s.cancel()` on the server's own context, which is not the one used here), so this goroutine and the underlying `WatchWriteEvents` poller goroutine in the SQL backend run forever after shutdown, leaking goroutines and DB pollers. The loop must select on a cancellable context and check `v, ok := <-events` to break on close.

findings.title: searchSupport.init starts its own WatchWriteEvents consumer, but server.initWatcher also starts one via the broadcaster — duplicate event streams and double-indexing
findings.body: `searchSupport.init` (line 203) calls `s.storage.WatchWriteEvents(watchctx)` and consumes events directly to update the search index. Separately, `server.Init` calls `s.initWatcher()` (server.go line 310) which calls `s.backend.WatchWriteEvents(s.ctx)` again (server.go line 755) to feed the broadcaster for client watches. At minimum this duplication should be acknowledged; functionally it works but is a performance/correctness smell (the two pollers may see events at different times, causing the index to lag behind the watch stream).
